title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance
abstract: arXiv:2611.25605v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI-generated bug reports have drawn criticism for unreliable claims and faulty reproducers that burden maintainers. However, as LLM capabilities improve, some maintainers have begun to express more positive views on AI use in bug reporting and maintenance. Understanding this evolution requires examining whether AI-involved reports are becoming more reliable, which uses of AI are associated with valid findings, and how maintainers investigate these reports and act on them. To this end, we conduct the first large-scale study of 120,918 bug reports from 101 open-source projects between January 2024 and September 2026, tracing AI involvement from discovery and reporting through validation and resolution. Our findings show that AI-involved reports become more complete over time, with a growing share of reports confirmed as valid. translated_title: 副驾驶还是罪魁祸首？AI如何改变开源软件的缺陷报告与维护
translated_abstract: AI生成的缺陷报告曾因不可靠的陈述和错误的复现步骤给维护者带来负担而饱受批评。然而，随着大语言模型（LLM）能力的提升，一些维护者开始对AI在缺陷报告与维护中的应用持更加积极的看法。理解这一演变需要考察：AI参与的报告是否正变得更加可靠，AI的哪些用途与有效的发现相关联，以及维护者如何调查这些报告并据此采取行动。为此，我们开展了首个大规模研究，分析了2024年1月至2026年9月期间来自101个开源项目的120,918份缺陷报告，追踪AI从发现、报告到验证和解决全过程中的参与情况。我们的研究结果表明，AI参与的报告随时间推移变得更加完整，被确认为有效的报告比例不断上升。在缺陷报告环节，AI用于复现和诊断与更高的报告有效性相关，而用于撰写报告……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次对101个开源项目中超过12万份缺陷报告进行大规模分析，发现AI参与的缺陷报告正变得越来越完整可靠，其中AI用于复现和诊断与更高的报告有效性相关。
en_tdlr: The first large-scale study of 120,918 bug reports from 101 open-source projects shows that AI-involved bug reports are becoming more complete and valid over time, with AI used for reproduction and diagnosis associated with higher report validity.
